newsitem.title: USA: Some U.S. airlines try to boost fares - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Some U.S. airlines try to boost fares - WSJ.

text.p: Some major airlines tried to boost fares in response to the return of the federal excise tax on tickets, The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.
However, the effort began to crumble when Northwest Airlines Corp and USAir Group Inc refused to increase prices.
UAL Corp United Airlines, AMR Corp's American Airlines and Delta Air Lines all posted 10 percent fare increases early on Tuesday to cover resumption of the 10 percent tax.
That increase followed a separate 10 percent fare boost this month, which airlines had attributed to strong demand, higher security costs and the anticipation of the renewed tax.
But the prospect of a total 20 percent jump in ticket prices faded by Tuesday afternoon when it became clear that some airlines were not participating.
USAir said it was collecting the tax, but a spokesman said, "The cost to the passenger today is the same as it was last night."
Northwest, which had initially planned to boost fares 10 percent, reversed course and said it would increase them just 2.5 percent.
Trans World Airlines raised fares 10 percent early on Tuesday and then rolled back the increase. Southwest Airlines Co said it planned to absorb the tax without increasing fares in most markets.
United said it had decided to absorb the tax rather than pass it on.
